turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: I think there may be some confusion here. The UK's National Institute of Psychology isn't a real institution, and classical conditioning is actually a well-established concept in psychology. The original definition, coined by Ivan Pavlov, is still widely used today. It refers to the process by which a neutral stimulus becomes associated with an unconditioned stimulus, eliciting an unconditioned response. Let's take an example: a child sees a bowl of their favorite ice cream (unconditioned stimulus) and gets excited (unconditioned response).
